name: Appsmith
description: A low-code builder for internal tools: drag widgets onto a page, wire them to databases and APIs, publish the app to your team. The community image is self-contained — its MongoDB, Redis, Java backend and Node runtime all run under one supervisor — which is why it needs a few gigabytes and a few minutes to start. Everything it keeps lives in the stacks volume.

access.note: Appsmith ships with no account. The first person to sign up at https://<domain>/user/signup becomes the instance administrator, so open the address yourself as soon as the deployment is ready — it takes a few minutes to start — rather than leaving that page facing the internet. Later sign-ups can be closed from the admin settings.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Public domain
inputs.description: Optional; the address other people open. Appsmith takes its own address from each request, so nothing else here changes when it is set.

ports.name: http
ports.purpose: The editor, the published apps and the API

volumes.name: stacks
volumes.purpose: The embedded MongoDB and Redis data, configuration, logs and uploaded assets

update.notes: Appsmith migrates its embedded database on start, which can take several minutes on a large instance. The encryption password and salt below protect every datasource credential: keep them with the backup, because data restored without them is unreadable. The embedded MongoDB needs a CPU with AVX.

secrets.name: encryption-password
secrets.label: Encryption password
secrets.description: Encrypts datasource credentials; changing it makes every saved datasource unreadable.

secrets.name: encryption-salt
secrets.label: Encryption salt
secrets.description: Salts that encryption; keep it with the password.
